Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Claire Huang (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Eve Martinez (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (Lumina Head of ML), Arjun Gupta (Lumina SRE), Liam O'Neill (Lumina Product), Zara Khan (Lumina DS)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Covered quality vs latency tradeoffs, memory/throughput impact, recommended rollout strategy, and pilot next steps. Action items agreed to share benchmark sheets, sample prompts, and schedule pilot kickoff.

[00:00] Claire Huang: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, uh quick intro, im claire, i'll run the walkthrough w/ samir, eve is here for product questions. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya Chen: good thanks, excited, we want to understand how much perf we can squeeze out for our real-time summarization pipeline without dropping quality, especially for low-latency customers.
[00:20] Samir Patel: awesome. quick FYI we'll show a couple of quant profiles we typically recommend: int8 (per-channel) and fp8 variants, and empirical quality vs latency numbers. also show how batching and kv-cache affect tail latency.
[00:32] Arjun Gupta: perfect. our SLA is 150ms p50 for short prompts, p95 can be up to 400ms but we'd like to get that down. and memory footprint is important because we want to run on Dedicated GPUs.
[00:45] Claire Huang: noted. quick qualification — what model are you currently using in prod?
[00:50] Liam O'Neill: we're on a 13B open model forked from wzl-mix (internal), trimmed, running on TF serving today; about 80 tokens typical request.
[01:05] Samir Patel: okay good context. int8 usually gives 2-3x throughput and significant mem reduction but can introduce minor quality regressions on sensitive prompts; fp8 often hits a sweet spot for quality with latency improvements but depends on kernel support and hardware.
[01:25] Zara Khan: when you say quality regressions, what magnitude are we talking — BLEU/ROUGE style or human evals?
[01:33] Samir Patel: good q. we do both. for summarization tasks like yours, INT8 occasionally shifts phrasing and can affect abstractive quality on ~2-6% of prompts by our automated metrics; human evals show acceptable differences for many customers but you — we recommend running your exact prompts.
[01:50] Maya Chen: makes sense, we can run your automated eval but want human spot checks.
[01:55] Claire Huang: totally. we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet (link: redwood.ai/benchmarks/lumina-int8) with metric breakdowns, delta columns, and raw latency logs.
[02:10] [interruption] Unknown Speaker: uh sorry brief noise i think
[02:15] Samir Patel: no worries. i'll demo two profiles now — FP8-fast (aggressive) and INT8-stable (conservative) — and show a side-by-side of p50/p95 and quality delta.
[02:28] [03:00] Samir Patel: (screen) okay here's the dashboard — this is a 13B model run on A100/dedicated cluster, INT8 profile used per-channel quant with calibration on 1k prompts. p50 dropped from 120ms to 45ms, p95 from 420ms to 220ms; quality delta in rouge-l is -3.2%.
[03:45] Maya Chen: that's pretty big for p95 improvement. what about FP8?
[03:50] Samir Patel: FP8 here gives p50 55ms, p95 180ms, rouge-l delta -1.0%, but note FP8 requires our new kernel path and on some older cards it's not available, and sometimes you see more jitter at tail due to fused ops.
[04:12] Arjun Gupta: kernel path — that's runtime changes right? do we need custom drivers?
[04:17] Samir Patel: no driver changes, it's within Redwood runtime; we select optimized kernels at runtime. for FP8 we use a quant-aware kernel set which benefits from newer cu* libs; if you're on older infra we fall back to INT8 or float.
[04:35] Liam O'Neill: what about cold start/kv-cache for chat style? we do long conversations for some customers.
[04:42] Samir Patel: KV cache helps heavily for long histories; batching helps throughput but increases tail latency. we demo both: with prefix caching, p95 for long contexts improves 30-40%. FP8 still helps but memory savings from int8 allow bigger batch sizes.
[05:05] [05:30] Claire Huang: question on evaluation: we recommend running both automated metrics and a small human eval set. Samir, can you explain the 'quality buckets' again?
[05:39] Samir Patel: sure — we break prompts into three buckets: sensitive (high risk for hallucination or safety), information-dense (long context summarization), and generic (chitchat). INT8 is fine for generic and some info-dense, we usually caution on sensitive prompts. FP8 tends to preserve more nuance so better for sensitive.
[06:05] Maya Chen: ok our summarization is information-dense with occasional legal/financial language — sounds like FP8 might be safer.
[06:13] Samir Patel: yes that aligns. you might run FP8 for sensitive routes and INT8 for low-risk bulk traffic — Redwood's routing policies can do that automatically.
[06:25] Zara Khan: how easy to roll out split traffic? can we canary one profile?
[06:30] Eve Martinez: absolutely — console supports route-level rollouts, canary %, and automatic rollback on quality regression tied to your evals. we have hooks to run your eval set periodically and alert.
[06:45] Arjun Gupta: security question: for Private (VPC) deployment can we still use FP8 kernels and does KMS integrate?
[06:53] Samir Patel: yes, Private supports the same runtime; KMS/HSM integrations are supported for key lifecycle. FP8 kernel support depends on the GPU drivers/libs but our Private image includes validated libs; we'll share the exact bill of materials in the security pack.
[07:10] Claire Huang: note — we'll attach SOC2/ISO docs in the follow-up (Claire action).
[07:15] [07:40] Samir Patel: back to numbers — here's a latency vs quality scatter: x-axis is p95 latency, y-axis is rouge-l delta. you can see FP8 is clustered lower delta with slightly higher p50 but better p95 in this sample. INT8 is lower p50 but tail varies more depending on batch.
[08:00] Liam O'Neill: what's the variance across hardware — A100 vs H100?
[08:06] Samir Patel: H100 tends to run FP8 faster due to tensor core support; A100 performs well for INT8. Our table in the spreadsheet lists hardware multipliers. we'll include a hardware matrix for your infra.
[08:25] Maya Chen: pricing implications? INT8 gives cost drops, but if we use mixed routing FP8 for sensitive traffic we still see savings overall?
[08:34] Claire Huang: yes typically customers see 25-50% unit cost reduction depending on split. we'll send a modeled cost sheet with scenarios for 20/80 FP8/INT8 split.
[08:50] Arjun Gupta: any gotchas for latency spikes? we've seen tail spikes in other runtimes during GC or model reloads.
[08:58] Samir Patel: we have warm pools, prefetching, and graceful degradation — automatic fallback to float-16 or smaller model variant if latency or errors spike. also pre-warmed reps on Dedicated to avoid cold-starts.
[09:15] Zara Khan: about quant calibration: you mentioned calibrating on 1k prompts — is that enough for our domain?
[09:21] Samir Patel: it's a starting point; for high-sensitivity workloads we recommend a 5-10k sample including edge cases. calibration is part of the Optimize toolkit and we can do it together in the pilot.
[09:35] Maya Chen: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we ideally want a 4-week pilot to validate latency and quality on production traffic.
[09:42] Claire Huang: typical pilot is 3-6 weeks: week 0 onboarding and data share, week 1-2 calibration and benchmarks, week 3-4 human eval and production canary. sounds like 4 weeks fits.
[09:55] [10:10] Samir Patel: quick demo clip — here's raw outputs on 10 sample prompts: left is float16 baseline, middle INT8, right FP8. you can see INT8 truncates a bit on multi-sentence summaries and FP8 maintains more structure.
[10:30] Maya Chen: hm yeah i can see that. for the ones with legal terms FP8 is closer.
[10:35] Liam O'Neill: how do we integrate this into our existing TF-serving flow? do you provide adapters?
[10:40] Eve Martinez: we provide API and SDKs, and for Private you can run our agent as a sidecar or use the Redwood dedicated runtime. POCs often use API first then move to Private or Dedicated once validated.
[10:58] Arjun Gupta: notes on observability — do you expose per-token timing and route-level traces?
[11:05] Samir Patel: yes token-level timing, token cost breakdown, per-model route dashboards, and tracing hooks. we can push logs to your S3 or to Splunk.
[11:20] Maya Chen: would like automated alerts if rouge score drops beyond threshold post-deploy.
[11:24] Claire Huang: that's supported — we'll wire the eval alerts to your Slack/PagerDuty.
[11:30] [12:00] Samir Patel: any other concerns?
[12:05] Maya Chen: just one — reproducibility of benchmarks; sometimes numbers differ when we run locally. how do you ensure parity?
[12:12] Samir Patel: we provide the raw runbook, seed configs, and the exact docker images/kernel versions. we also offer a validation run where we reproduce results on your infra as part of the pilot.
[12:28] Liam O'Neill: ok good. can we get a sample config for doing FP8 to validate locally?
[12:33] Claire Huang: yes we'll share a sample config and a step-by-step. Claire action to send that and the security pack.
[12:40] Zara Khan: timeline for next week — we can gather prompts and traffic slices by Tuesday.
[12:46] Claire Huang: great. Samir — you'll do the benchmark runs and share sheets by next Thursday?
[12:50] Samir Patel: yes i can target 2026-12-02 for the runs and logs.
[12:56] [13:10] Claire Huang: recap quick — next steps: Samir share benchmarks and logs; Claire send pricing and security docs; Lumina upload prompts; schedule pilot kickoff week of Dec 6. any objections?
[13:25] Maya Chen: none, thanks everyone.
[13:30] Arjun Gupta: thanks, looking forward.
[13:35] Claire Huang: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
